item.text: The issue is in the emphasis-preprocessing mask: it replaces escaped punctuation before it masks code spans. So the backslash immediately before the closing backtick is treated as escaping that backtick during emphasis detection, even though it is literal code content. I’m adjusting the mask order so code spans are hidden first.

item.text:
The cause was the emphasis mask treating the backslash before a code span’s closing backtick as an escape. I changed [Lexer.ts](/C:/Users/USER/Downloads/agent-test/limit/codexdev_t6t3_r5/work/src/Lexer.ts:396) to mask code spans before escaped punctuation, so backslashes inside code no longer affect emphasis parsing outside it.

I couldn’t verify the change with the requested checks: `npm run build:esbuild` failed because esbuild could not access a parent directory, and `npm run test:specs` then failed because the build hadn’t created `lib/marked.esm.js`.
